speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to help narrow down the cause, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they came on suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's Thumb (Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injury) of the Right Ring Finger.

*Note: Based on the mechanism of injury (forceful abduction/pulling of the finger during a sports collision) and the resulting pain/swelling, this is the most likely diagnosis. While "Gamekeeper's Thumb" typically refers to the thumb, the pathophysiology applies equally to the ring finger in this context. I would recommend a X-Ray to rule out fracture or dislocation and a MRI if ligament rupture is suspected.*

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
